plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of competitors' strategies. Since the winner pays the second-highest bid (not their own bid), there's no incentive to shade the bid up or down—overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if I win, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. This holds regardless of other bidders' beliefs about my strategy, since my payment doesn't depend on my own bid amount when I win. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $39.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because the payment is determined by the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks negative profit while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since other bidders are rational, they will also recognize this and likely bid their true values. Therefore, my optimal strategy is simply to bid exactly my value of $20, ensuring I win only when profitable and pay a fair price when I do.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if you bid your true value, you win whenever the highest competing bid is below your value, and win only when it's profitable (since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid). This holds even if others deviate from truthful bidding. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $20.
